falsifiers.statement: RouteCandidate.__post_init__ validates candidate_id only as a generic identifier and does not recompute the route: digest from the remaining candidate fields. Therefore a directly constructed or dataclasses.replace-produced RouteCandidate can carry an arbitrary syntactically valid candidate_id while all other fields remain valid. Current tests cover classification tampering and deterministic route_task generation, but not candidate-id self-consistency.
falsifiers.minimal_regression: candidate = route_task(...); forged = replace(candidate, candidate_id='route:' + 'f' * 64); current constructor accepts forged unless candidate-id self-consistency is explicitly enforced.
falsifiers.risk: A downstream Native Child ABI or handoff consumer that treats candidate_id as an integrity binding without recomputing/validating it can accept identity/content divergence. This does not create current runtime/effect authority, but it weakens the intended fail-closed typed boundary before F2-WP-601 consumption.

contradictions: The active WP600 scope requires fail-closed rejection when identity/policy data is invalid, while the emitted RouteCandidate object currently has no self-consistency fence tying candidate_id back to its exact content.
completion_deficit: Add one exact regression for direct/replace candidate_id tampering and choose one canonical trust-boundary repair: recompute/compare candidate_id from candidate fields, or make downstream consumption require a validator that performs the same recomputation. Preserve RouteCandidate as candidate-only; grant no runtime/effect/completion authority.
next_exact_action: Active WP600 mutation authority should re-enter current main, absorb this falsifier if still applicable, add the smallest fail-closed candidate-id binding repair plus regression, then require repository-hosted CI before bounded component acceptance. F2-WP-601 must not consume RouteCandidate as identity-authentic solely because candidate_id is present.
